relevance_note: Case report of one Chinese boy with Majeed syndrome and compound heterozygous LPIN2 variants ("Molecular testing identified a paternal splicing donor site variant c.2327 + 1G > C and a maternal frameshift variant"), plus a literature table of 14 previously reported patients.
method_note: Read the whole paper; a Python script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON and took every span and table-derived value verbatim from the Markdown (the paper uses thin spaces U+2009 inside variant strings and ages; these are preserved). Table 1 (literature summary, 14 rows) was transcribed by script and checked against the table row by row; it has no label column, so rows are labelled "Table 1 row k". Its author cells are blank for rows continuing the author above (rows 3-7 Ferguson [3], 9 Herlin [4], 11 Rao [5], 13 Moussa [6]); source_reference_in_review for those rows quotes the author cell of the first row of the group plus the row itself. Rows 3 and 5 are byte-identical lines. Concatenated cells (e.g. "Mild feverMicrocytosisSweet syndrome") were split at the evident item boundaries. Laboratory values in Table 1 printed as bare numbers (ESR, CRP, Hb) were not turned into observed/excluded features or checklist items, because the table does not label them as elevated or low; only labelled items ("Neutropenia", "High inflammatory") were used. "Relative with psoriasis" describes a relative, not the row person, and was not recorded. "Frequent blood transfusion" was recorded as treatment. "Fever" without "recurrent" and "Microcytosis"/"Dyserythropoietic anemia" were recorded as features but not mapped to the checklist items recurrent fever, microcytic anemia or dyserythropoiesis on bone marrow. "No skin lesions" (Moussa rows) excludes the narrower checklist item neutrophilic dermatosis. Merges: the Discussion sentence "The proband was a 3-year-old girl with Majeed syndrome [2]" (first report of c.2327 + 1G > C in an Arabic family) was treated as Table 1 row 1 (Mosawi [2], F, 3 y, c.2327 + 1G > C), and "RAO reported a 15-year-old boy ... mild neutropenia [5]" as Table 1 row 10 (Rao [5], M, 15 y, mild neutropenia). "Mosawi reported an Arabic female ... mild neutropenia (1080/mm^3) in the neonatal period [3]" was kept as a separate person ("ref [3] patient") because its reference number and neutrophil count differ from Table 1 row 1 (750/mm^3); it may be the same person as Table 1 row 1 or a Ferguson [3] row. "Majeed reported a Palestinian Arab boy ... [12]" is included as "ref [12] patient"; the paper does not state his diagnosis explicitly (the paragraph compares him with previously reported Majeed syndrome cases), so disease_label is not reported. Parents: DNA was obtained from both parents and the paper calls the variants "paternal" and "maternal"; rows "father of patient" and "mother of patient" carry the respective variant, with zygosity, pathogenicity and inheritance not reported for them. Proband: "no hepatosplenomegaly" was recorded as such and not used to exclude hepatomegaly or splenomegaly separately; normal abdominal ultrasound, cardiac ultrasound and other normal investigations are recorded as written (D-27) and exclude nothing more specific. "no physical pain" / "no limbs pain" exclude bone pain and joint pain; "no physical pain, swelling, or movement disorders" excludes joint or limb swelling; "no rash" excludes neutrophilic dermatosis. CRMO is not reported for the proband (only "without severe CRMO"; no MRI). In-silico splice prediction and population frequency were not treated as functional evidence. Contradictions/oddities in the paper: Table 1 cites Moussa as [6] but reference [6] is Monies et al. and Moussa is [7]; the Moussa rows print "c.2327 + 1G > Cp.s734 L", pairing the splice variant with the protein change printed for c.2201C > T in the Ferguson rows; the text cites Mosawi as [3] while the table gives Mosawi [2] (reference [3] is Ferguson); Herlin rows print an upper-case "P." protein prefix; Fig. 1 legend says "PLIN2". The gene symbol for Table 1 rows is taken from the Fig. 2 legend (variants previously reported in the literature on LPIN2), since the table itself does not name the gene.
